sources.title: Animal Classification - Biology LibreTexts (CK-12)
facts_used: 9 major phyla each contain at least 10,000 species
Invertebrates comprise at least 95% of all animal species
Phylum Chordata includes both vertebrate and invertebrate members (tunicates, lancelets)
The first 8 phyla contain only invertebrates

sources.title: Features Used to Classify Animals - Lumen Learning (SUNY Biology)
facts_used: Three body symmetry types: asymmetry (Porifera), radial (Cnidaria), bilateral (most phyla)
Body cavity types: acoelomate (flatworms), pseudocoelomate (roundworms), coelomate (annelids, arthropods, etc.)
Diploblasts have 2 tissue layers (endoderm, ectoderm); triploblasts have 3 (add mesoderm)
Protostomes: arthropods, mollusks, annelids; Deuterostomes: chordates, echinoderms
Cephalization: concentration of nervous system at anterior end, enabled by bilateral symmetry
Radial symmetry suits stationary/slow organisms; bilateral suits active movers

sources.title: Animal Phyla - Wikiversity
facts_used: Porifera means 'pore bearer', ~5,000+ species
Cnidaria means 'stinging nettle', ~11,000 species, cnidocytes
Platyhelminthes means 'flat worms', ~25,000 species
Nematoda means 'thread like', 80,000-1,000,000 species
Annelida means 'little ring', ~22,000 species
Arthropoda means 'jointed foot', 1,134,000+ species, chitin exoskeleton
Mollusca means 'thin shell', ~85,000 species, muscular foot and mantle
Echinodermata means 'spiny skin', ~7,000 living species, five-fold radial symmetry
Chordata means 'cord', ~100,000+ species, hollow dorsal nervous chord
Total approximately 34 animal phyla representing ~1.9 million described species

sources.title: Phylum - Wikipedia
facts_used: Arthropoda estimated 3.7 million species (most sources cite >1 million described)
Mollusca ~118,061 species
Chordata/Craniata ~85,432 vertebrate species
About 35 known animal phyla total

sources.title: Animal Phyla | Chart, Types & Characteristics - Study.com
facts_used: Within the animal kingdom there are 35 total phyla, 9 are the most well known
Vertebrates divided into 5 groups: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish, and Amphibians

sources.title: Common Student Misconceptions - Conceptual Academy
facts_used: Common misconception: only vertebrates are animals
Students often don't consider sponges, jellyfish, worms, insects as animals
Common misconception: bugs/insects are not animals

standards_data.full_text: The student will investigate and understand that organisms can be classified based on shared characteristics. Key ideas include the distinguishing characteristics of kingdoms; the major animal and plant phyla; and the use of classification systems.
essential_knowledge_addressed: Distinguishing characteristics of the 9 major animal phyla
The major animal phyla and their representative organisms
The use of classification systems (taxonomy, body plan features)
How physical characteristics enable organisms to survive (structural adaptations by phylum)
